stories.title: Pope praises young people's 'energy and commitment' at huge open-air Mass in Paris
stories.standfirst: Around 700,000 people gathered in central Paris to hear the Catholic leader speak and offer prayer.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Pope Leo XIV travelled down the Champs-Élysées in his popemobile before a huge open-air Mass in central Paris. Hundreds of thousands of people gathered to greet him, with over half a million expected at Place de la Concorde. Earlier, the Pope visited a refugee support centre and met migrants. French President Emmanuel Macron met the Pope on Friday but is avoiding the Masses to respect state secularism rules. However, his wife, the prime minister, and several presidential candidates attended.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The Church believes the large crowds show growing spirituality in France and Europe. During his visit, the Pope urged dignity and peace, praised the role of women, and warned against losing humanity to artificial intelligence.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: On Sunday, 150,000 people will attend Mass with the Pope in Lourdes. On Monday, he will visit Metz to honour Robert Schuman, a founding father of the European Union.

stories.title: Decap is the man behind the drums behind your favorite song
stories.standfirst: I don't think I'm going to hurt anyone's feelings by pointing out that Decap doesn't have the name recognition of Kendrick Lamar, Olivia Rodrigo, or Charli XCX.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Record producer Nicholas Piantedosi, known as Decap, was interviewed about his work and music tools. He created the Drums That Knock sample pack series, which debuted in 2016 and is now on its eleventh instalment. He discussed his creative process, his favourite software Ableton Live, and his 1998 sampler.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Decap's sounds feature on tracks by major artists including Kendrick Lamar and Bad Bunny, as well as the Oppenheimer film score. Producer Kenneth Blume noted that Decap changed a million lives with a single snare. Decap also criticised gear gatekeeping, explaining that anyone with a computer has everything they need.

stories.title: Burnham announces scheme to help first-time buyers onto housing ladder
stories.standfirst: The prime minister says he wants people without support from the "bank of mum and dad" to receive help.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has announced a housing scheme called Your First Home for first-time buyers in England. The initiative offers a 20% equity loan on a new build home to buyers with a 2.5% deposit. The loan includes an initial interest-free period, with funding coming from existing budgets and housing developers.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The government aims to help buyers who lack financial help from family and give builders confidence to supply new properties. This announcement comes as new home construction has declined, leaving the government behind on its target to build 1.5 million homes by the next election.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Further details about the scheme will be revealed in next month's Budget. Pre-registration for buyers will open before the end of the year.
